14. The appellate Court, on the other hand, came to the finding that as per C.S. khatian Gani Mia (Guno Mia) was in exclusive possession of plot No.3182. The Appellate Court also found that in the C.S. khatian the four boundaries of the plot were clearly given which exclusively proved that Gani Mia, the C.S. recorded tenant was in exclusive possession of the suit plot No.3182. The appellate Court held that the suit land did not belong to Oli Mia but that it actually belonged to Gani Mia, who sold it to Lal Mia, who again sold it to Najir Ahmed. The Appellate Court also held that as Najir Ahmed had succeeded in proving his title by way of purchase on the basis of registered deed (exhibit-2ka) the initial presumption attached to R.S. khatian, exhibit-1(ka) was rebutted. The appellate Court also held that Najir Ahmed as tenure-holder in R.S. plot No.4429 (suit plot) was entitled to transfer the same by way of settlement which he did accordingly by executing patta exhibit-3 dated 18.07.1925, by which 18 gondas of land were transferred to Abdur Rahman. The appellate Court also held that the allegations of fraud by Najir Ahmed was not proved by cogent evidence and that the appellate Court also held that one who alleged fraud must bear the burden of proving it and the burden is comparatively heavier when it is against old registered documents. The appellate Court also held that by three documents (exhibits-2, 2ka and 3) no land of Oli Mia was attracted and that the chance of fraud in view of the given circumstances seemed to be too remote. Therefore, the appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs had been able to prove their title to and possession in the suit land and accordingly, the appellate Court decreed the suit. 

 20. The aforesaid findings proved that the suit land did not belong to Oli Mia but it actually belonged to Gani Mia, who sold it to Lal Mia, who again sold it to Najir Ahmed. As Najir Ahmed has succeeded in proving his title by way of purchase on the basis of registered deed (exhibit-2ka) the initial presumption attached to the R.S. khatian exhibit-1(ka) was rebutted. Therefore, Najir Ahmed was legally entitle to settled the suit land to Abdur Rahman by exhibit-3, the registered patta dated 18.07.1925. The appellate Court on consideration of evidence on record found that the allegation of fraud was not proved in obtaining the suit land by the plaintiffs. The appellate Court also discussed the evidence adduced by P.Ws.1, 2 and 3 and found that they could prove that the Abdur Rahman was in actual possession of the suit land. The appellate Court also noted that P.Ws.2 and 3 were not cross-examined by the defendants in respect of their evidence as regards possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The appellate Court also noted that the defendants did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence during the trial. The appellate Court also considered exhibits-4 and 4ka, the rent receipts in respect of the suit land and found that the plaintiffs paid rent before filing of the suit and that rent receipt not only proved possession of the plaintiffs but also proved as collateral evidence of title to the suit land. The appellate Court noted that respondent No.3 filed three rent receipts relating to P.S. plot No.3080 for an area of .08, .22, .10 and .05 acre of land and that from those rent receipts, the plaintiffs' claim of possession was not affected so far as regards the quantum of land in P.S. khatian No.3082. The appellate Court also held that the defendants had not come out with positive proof regarding exclusive possession of P.S. plot No.4429 and as such, their onus was not discharged.
